feedback.problem:
Let $V={R}^{3}$ be the vector space equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x,y⟩={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.
$$

If $x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ and 
$y=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ k \\ 5\end{aligned}]$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V,$ then $k=$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $x$ and $y$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & ={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{3}{y}_{3} \\  & =0\cdot 3+3\cdot ((-2)\cdot k)+3\cdot (2\cdot 5) \\  & =0-6k+30 \\  & =-6k+30\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $⟨x,y⟩=0$ and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & =0 \\ -6k+30 & =0 \\ 6k & =30 \\ k & =5\end{aligned}
$$
